messages.subject: [R-sig-QA] Validation of an R installation
messages.body_plain:
I am visiting Martin Maechler at ETH in Zurich, Switzerland for a month. 
  During this time I will also visit Tony Rossini and others at Novartis 
in Basel for a day.  One of the topics that I will discuss with Tony and 
have discussed extensively with Martin is ways in which we can help 
those useRs who face questions of whether R is "validated".  There was 
some discussion on R-Help about this recently and there has also been 
discussion in the past both on- and off-list.

Those who have compiled R from the sources may realize that "make check" 
and "make check-all" apply an extensive and ever-growing series of test 
cases to a version of R.  The same is true of R CMD check for packages.

In general a binary version of R or binary versions of packages do not 
include the tests directory.  There is no need - the tests are run at 
the time that the binary version is created.  However, it would be 
reasonable for a useR to have a mechanism to perform such tests on 
his/her installed version of R when desired, even if the version is from 
a binary installation.  One way we felt this could be achieved is to 
create a 'validate' package that contains the files used for the tests. 
  A useR can install the package then run the tests.  I believe that 
this would do substantially more validation of R that what is done for 
commercial statistical packages.

I have also proposed to Martin that we produce a document that describes 
the software development process for R, including the QA tools that are 
applied throughout the development process.

Others, especially Henric Nilsson, Frank Harrell Jr., Tony Rossini, and 
Jim Garrett, have proposed producing a document similar to the "white 
papers" produced by commercial companies specifically addressing the FDA 
guidelines in Title 21, Code of Federal Regulations, Part 11.  We hope 
that such efforts could be facilitated by what we propose.

Martin has proposed in private mail to Henric that we use the R-SIG-QA 
email list to communicate about this effort.  I think it would be an 
excellent use of this list and I hope others agree.

I include a list of topics that we felt might be discussed in a document 
about the development process for R core.  Suggestions and comments on 
this list and on the general idea of a validate package are welcome.

		   Quality assurance methods for R

			     R Core Team

Composition of R-Core Team

Access to the source code repository

Versions of R available - R-release, R-patched, R-devel

Routine tests applied during the development process

Release process
    Tests performed during release

Building R from source code

  configuration process (autoconf)
  range of tests covered by 'make check'
  range of tests covered by 'make check-all'

Binary installations

  Windows

    Configuration
    Checks performed on binary builds

  OS X for the Macintosh

    Configuration
    Checks performed on binary builds

Checking of packages on CRAN

  Daily package checking

Special capabilities

  Memory leak detection through valgrind

"War stories"

  Bugs found in other software (e.g. Lapack)

One qualification that needs to be done is an "installation
qualification".  I.e. there ought to be a means by which I can run a
function after the installation,
    
   DoesMyInstallationFollowRCOREguidelines()

which might check for permissions, library versioning/mismatches,  etc.

Even better, this would run similar functions on 3rd party packages
which might provide, in addition to correctness of the current
installation (by that I'm more concerned with libraries as well as
rerunning parts of  R CMD check, if such a thing were possible on
installed packages as well as giving  numerical confirmation that the
results are within numerical tolerance of error).

Can we comment on the role of the R Foundation in supporting
continuing development of R?  Strong evidence (of course, not
guaranteed!) of continuing development is one issue in quality
assurance.

Thanks for raising this a bit, Doug.  I've got a half written paper on
issues for the use of academic and open source (there is a
distinction!) in a regulated production environment, that I'll need to
put out.

Also, the origin of a quality assurance and FDA-compliance white
paper/statement would have to come from the "vendor", i.e. R-Core, for
companies to feel comfortable with it.

-- 
best,
-tony

"Commit early,commit often, and commit in a repository from which we can easily
roll-back your mistakes" (AJR, 4Jan05).

A.J. Rossini

Following up on my own post, here is an internal response from Andreas
Krause (of Krause & Olson fame), our local reluctant expert on
validation.   Please don't hold it against him, I was going to
threaten access to the expresso machine if he didn't comment :-).

> Tony,
>
>this list looks good. Going by my experiences so far,
>
>the validate() function in Splus is really useful
>and so is the white paper that Insightful released on their quality
>assurance policy and techniques.
>That's the major emphasis.
>
>Then there is typically a vendor audit (actually including a visit to the
>vendor), and here I'm not clear what that might mean for R.
>I have actually suggested to Insightful that they become some sort of Red
>Hat or SuSe for R, and they seem to have discussed it.
>I would put that question forward to the group. Elvis Miller (XLS
>solutions, isn't it?) might be interested, too.
>Maybe Ueli can comment on what people actually do during a vendor audit
>visit.
>
>Finally, a validation needs to take place for every new version, and
>that's a pain given R's fairly frequent updates (compared to S-Plus and
>SAS at least). Another point of discussion (POD).
>
>If we sort these points out, we should be very close to making it come
>true.


best,
-tony
